extracted.intended_audience: creative agencies, brands, marketers and entrants considering submission to the Cannes Lions Awards
extracted.subtask_description: High-level criteria and standards used to frame and communicate what the Cannes Lions Awards recognise — e.g., creative excellence, effectiveness, organisational creative capability, integrity rules, and category-level innovations such as data/AI. This page is the awards landing/overview rather than a detailed judging scorecard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lions honour the world's most groundbreaking creative work, setting the global benchmark for marketing and communications excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames 'creative excellence' as the core purpose of the Awards: winning a Lion is described as a career-defining achievement and an opportunity to 'share your work with the world' and 'make history.' This criterion emphasises originality, boundary-pushing ideas and industry-leading creative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Across a breadth of specialist categories, the Lions celebrate creative excellence and effectiveness in every sector and discipline of the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness is presented alongside creative excellence as a principal standard — work should demonstrate impact and contribute to business or communications goals. The page notes that winners receive 'visibility, credibility and a confirmation that our disruptive ideas drive their businesses closer to achieving their strategic goals.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational creative capability (Creative Brand Lion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Creative Brand Lion celebrates how brands strategically use creativity across their organisation by recognising the systems, cultures and capabilities that make world-class work inevitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion expands assessment beyond single campaigns to evaluate the systems, culture and capabilities within a brand or organisation that enable consistent, high-quality creative output. It signals rewards for strategic, structural and cultural excellence in creativity, not only individual execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries and the Awards process are governed by LIONS Integrity Standards (supported by a downloadable LIONS Integrity Handbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the page does not list the standards' specifics, it explicitly points entrants and stakeholders to the Integrity Standards and Handbook, indicating that adherence to those integrity rules is required and relevant to award consideration and the awards' legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data, innovation and AI
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme includes a refresh to the Creative Data Lion and the introduction of new AI subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals a substantive criterion around data-driven creativity and innovative application of AI: categories and judging will recognise excellence where data or AI meaningfully informs creative work. The page does not provide scoring detail but marks these as distinct, category-level evaluation focuses for 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and evolving industry disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards and juries reflect evolving industry disciplines and increased representation from regions and types of organisations (e.g., more disciplines, brands, independent agencies, increased representation from Africa, Pacific, MENA and LATAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While primarily describing jury composition and scope, this implies an evaluative emphasis on global perspectives and cross-disciplinary work. It signals that submissions will be considered within a broader, more diverse global benchmark of creativity.
